name: Flaxseed
notes:
Whole flaxseed (linseed). Nutrition is USDA.

Yield (~1.3 t/ha) is the FAO world average; Canada, Kazakhstan and Russia are the main growers, on prairie and steppe. Water is the Mekonnen & Hoekstra global average. Emissions average two sources: Poore & Nemecek's oilseed range (1.4) and the Dutch RIVM database (1.68, including transport to Europe).

Soil erosion, CO2 capture and fertilizer are generic estimates for annual temperate oilseeds rather than flax-specific data.

name: Sesame Seeds
notes:
Whole dried sesame seeds, nutrition from USDA. Yield is FAOSTAT world (~500 kg/ha), a low yield because most sesame is grown by smallholders in Sudan, India, Myanmar, Ethiopia, China and Nigeria. Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra (9,371 L/kg), very high because of the low yield.

Poore & Nemecek have no sesame figure, so emissions (~4.0 kg CO2e/kg) are a confidence-1 guess: flaxseed's per-hectare footprint divided by sesame's yield. Pesticide, fertilizer and compound rates are copied from flaxseed at confidence 1.
land_types_note: Sudan (~15%), India (~12%), Myanmar (~11%), Ethiopia, China, Nigeria and Burkina Faso, mostly rain-fed savanna.

name: Hemp Seeds
notes:
Hulled hemp seeds ('hemp hearts'), nutrition from USDA. FAOSTAT's hempseed yield (~1,000 kg/ha) is whole seed, so it is converted to a hulled basis at 35% (confidence 1 guess from dehulling studies), giving ~350 kg/ha; availability and water are converted the same way. Canada grows ~72% of the world's hempseed (excluding China, which FAOSTAT doesn't report separately).

Poore & Nemecek have no hemp figure, so emissions (~5.7 kg CO2e/kg) are a confidence-1 guess: flaxseed's per-hectare footprint divided by the hulled yield. Pesticide, fertilizer and compound rates are copied from flaxseed at confidence 1.
land_types_note: Canadian prairies (~72%), plus Australia, Russia, Chile, the US and Ukraine.

name: Chia Seeds
notes:
Dried chia seeds, nutrition from USDA. FAOSTAT and the water-footprint reports have no chia, so yield (~600 kg/ha) and availability (~160 Gg) come from reported national production and area figures (confidence 2 and 1). Paraguay (~80–90 kt), Bolivia and Argentina grow most chia, much of it newly cleared Chaco land.

Water is borrowed from sesame (9,371 L/kg; confidence 1), a drought-tolerant seed crop with a similar low yield. Emissions (~3.3 kg CO2e/kg) are a confidence-1 guess from flaxseed's per-hectare footprint divided by chia's yield. Pesticide, fertilizer and compound rates are copied from flaxseed at confidence 1.
land_types_note: Paraguay, Bolivia and Argentina (the Chaco and nearby savanna), plus Mexico, Nicaragua and Colombia.

name: Pumpkin Seeds
notes:
Dried pumpkin seed kernels (pepitas), nutrition from USDA. This assumes hull-less (Styrian-type) oil pumpkins, so the kernel is the whole harvested seed. FAOSTAT has no pumpkin-seed item, so yield (~600 kg/ha, from Austrian oil-pumpkin yields) and availability (~200 Gg) are educated guesses at confidence 1.

Water is derived by dividing a pumpkin crop's water per hectare by the seed yield (~8,568 L/kg, confidence 1). name: Cocoa (Unsweetened Baking Chocolate)
notes:
Unsweetened cocoa mass (baking chocolate, ground roasted cocoa nibs including their cocoa butter), nutrition from USDA. FAOSTAT's cocoa bean yield (~480 kg/ha) is converted to cocoa mass at 0.8 kg per kg of dry beans (shell and moisture lost in roasting and winnowing; educated estimate), ≈ 380 kg/ha. Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana grow about 60% of the world's cocoa, much of it on land cleared from tropical forest.

Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra's cocoa paste figure (24,238 L/kg). Poore & Nemecek only publish dark chocolate (46.65 kg CO2e/kg, mostly land-use change), so the cocoa mass emissions (~63.2) are derived from it: (46.65 − 28% sugar × 3.2 − 1.5 processing) ÷ 70% cocoa, confidence 2. Fertilizer (~15 kg/ha) reflects the very low use in West Africa. Pesticide (~2.5 kg/ha) and the compounds are confidence-1 guesses; the usual copper fungicides aren't in the toxicity table. Availability is FAOSTAT cocoa bean production × 0.8.
land_types_note: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana (~60%), Indonesia, Ecuador, Cameroon, Nigeria and Brazil, mostly smallholder plots in humid tropical forest zones.
